hero.headline: Anthropic raises $65 billion, surpassing OpenAI in valuation
hero.body:
Anthropic completed a $65 billion Series H funding round, bringing its post-money valuation to $965 billion and making it more valuable than OpenAI. The AI company's latest fundraising represents one of the largest venture capital rounds in tech history.

The seven cofounders of Anthropic are now worth a combined $116 billion following the funding round. The company develops AI systems including Claude, competing directly with OpenAI's ChatGPT and other large language models.

Wedbush analyst Dan Ives described Anthropic's growth as just the tip of the spear for the broader AI rally taking place across the technology sector. The massive valuation reflects investor enthusiasm for AI development, though it also raises questions about whether such sky-high pricing benefits ordinary investors.

The funding comes as AI companies continue to attract enormous capital despite ongoing debates about the technology's economic impact and competitive landscape. Anthropic was founded by former OpenAI executives who left to start their own AI safety-focused company.

The new valuation places Anthropic among the most valuable private technology companies globally. The funding will reportedly support further development of AI models and expansion of computing infrastructure needed for training increasingly complex systems.

OpenAI had previously been considered the leader in generative AI valuation, making Anthropic's surpassing of its valuation a significant shift in the competitive landscape. Both companies are racing to develop more capable AI systems while navigating regulatory scrutiny and public debate over AI safety.

The Series H round attracted investment from major backers, though specific investor names were not disclosed in available reports. The scale of investment reflects confidence in Anthropic's technology and business model despite the broader questions facing the AI industry about sustainable business models and paths to profitability.

cards.headline: Iranian Missile Strikes US Base in Kuwait During Peace Negotiations
cards.body:
US Strikes Kill Scores of Children at Iranian School

A US Tomahawk missile struck a primary school in Minab, Iran, killing more than 168 people, mostly children, according to video evidence and investigative analysis. The strike occurred on February 28 when US-Israeli operations against Iran began.

The missile hit the Shajareh Tayyebeh primary school as it targeted an adjacent Islamic Revolutionary Guards naval compound. The strike demolished approximately half the school building, killing scores of seven- to 12-year-old girls attending morning classes.

Video footage released by the Iranian news agency Mehr and verified by the investigative collective Bellingcat shows a Tomahawk missile striking the Minab compound. Munitions experts confirmed the weapon's origin. NR Jenzen-Jones, director of Armament Research Services, stated: "The video shows a Tomahawk missile striking a target. Given the belligerents, that indicates it is a US strike, as Israel is not known to possess Tomahawk missiles."

Jenzen-Jones added that the weapon was clearly not an Iranian Soumar missile, which has a distinctive external engine located toward the rear on the underside. He noted: "Despite various claims circulating online, the munition in question is clearly not an Iranian Soumar missile."

The evidence includes verified videos from the Guardian, photographs of the aftermath, and satellite imagery showing at least four buildings were hit during the strikes: the school and three IRGC compound buildings. Though the school building was once part of the wider IRGC complex, it had been walled off from the compound for at least eight years with clear educational markers visible in satellite images, including playing fields and colorful wall murals.

US President Donald Trump disputed responsibility for the school bombing. "In my opinion, based on what I've seen, that was done by Iran," Trump said on Sunday without providing evidence. He suggested Iranian munitions were inaccurate and claimed Iran was responsible.

US military spokespeople said they are "investigating" the strike. UNESCO described the school bombing as a "grave violation" of international law. Human Rights Watch called for an investigation into whether the strike constitutes a war crime.

The incident represents a significant escalation in the conflict between the United States and Iran. US military bases throughout the Gulf region have historically been potential targets in any confrontation with Iran. The strike on a civilian school has drawn international scrutiny and raised questions about adherence to laws protecting educational facilities during armed conflict.

The bombing adds to mounting tensions between Washington and Tehran as diplomatic efforts continue to address regional security concerns and the strategic Strait of Hormuz, through which significant portions of global oil supplies pass.

cards.headline: Trump requests changes to Iran deal his negotiators reached
cards.body:
President Trump has asked for several amendments to a deal framework his negotiators reached with Iranian counterparts, according to administration officials. The president wants the agreement finalized soon but is seeking to strengthen key provisions, particularly around Iran's nuclear program.

Trump's request has launched another round of negotiations between the parties that could extend several days. The tentative agreement reached this week would extend the current ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz if approved.

Trump announced on Saturday that an agreement had been "largely negotiated" after calls with Pakistani mediators, Gulf allies, and Israel. He posted on his social media platform that "final aspects and details" of a "memorandum of understanding" were still being discussed and would be announced shortly.

According to reports, the draft agreement includes provisions that the strait would reopen without tolls during a 60-day ceasefire extension, while Iran would be able to sell oil freely. Negotiations on curbing Iran's nuclear program would occur over 30 to 60 days. In exchange, the U.S. would lift its blockade on Iranian ports.

However, Iran's Fars news agency, which is close to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, disputed Trump's characterization of progress. The agency reported that "the management of the Strait, determining the route, time, method of passage, and issuing permits will continue to be the monopoly and discretion of the Islamic Republic of Iran," and said Trump's assertion that an agreement was nearly final was "inconsistent with reality."

Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif congratulated Trump on his peace efforts and said Pakistan hoped to host another round of talks between the U.S. and Iran soon. Pakistan's army chief, Syed Asim Munir, has been a key figure in the negotiations, holding recent meetings in Tehran with Iranian leaders.

Trump has described his negotiation strategy as conditional, telling media outlets he would only sign a deal "where we get everything we want," adding that if an agreement was not reached, the U.S. would begin striking Iran again.

The potential deal has sparked criticism from Republican hawks, particularly former officials from Trump's first term. Mike Pompeo, who served as CIA director and secretary of state, denounced the rumored terms as too similar to the 2015 nuclear deal negotiated under President Barack Obama, which Trump withdrew from in 2018.

Former Obama negotiators defended the approach differently. Robert Malley responded to criticism by stating that while the current deal might not follow the exact path his team would have taken, "if this deal brings an end to an unlawful, unjustifiable war, to the senseless loss of life and destruction, and to the cascading global economic fallout, I am quite sure we'd willingly accept it over the alternative."

The timing for final approval remains uncertain as negotiations continue.

cards.headline: Zelensky warns of major Russian attacks within 48 hours
cards.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said intelligence shared by the U.S. and European allies indicates Russia will launch major attacks in the next two days.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is preparing for a significant Russian military attack expected within the next 48 hours, based on intelligence from the U.S. and European allies. He anticipates the strikes could occur at night, either immediately or within the following day.

Zelensky warned of major attacks coming from Russia in the near term.

cards.headline: Israeli forces capture medieval castle in deepest Lebanon incursion in 26 years
cards.body:
Israeli troops have captured Beaufort Castle, a Crusader fortress in southern Lebanon, in what marks the country's deepest military incursion into Lebanese territory in more than 26 years. The castle, also known as Qalaat al-Shakif, sits on a mountain ridge near the city of Nabatiyeh and commands sweeping views across southern Lebanon and northern Israel.

The fortress dates back to the 1100s and has changed hands multiple times throughout history. Sultan Baibars captured it in 1268, and it has proven valuable in modern conflicts between Israel and Lebanon. Israeli forces previously took control of the castle in 1982 during their occupation of southern Lebanon, which lasted until 2000.

Defense Minister Israel Katz announced the capture on his Telegram channel, writing: "Forty-four years after the heroic Battle of Beaufort, and on this day commemorating the soldiers who fell in the First Lebanon War (1982), our troops have returned to the summit of Beaufort and once again raised the Israeli flag there." Photographs showed Israeli troops outside the castle with the Israeli flag raised above the citadel.

The operation came after intense fighting and airstrikes in surrounding villages where Israeli forces engaged with Hezbollah members. The Israeli military stated that Hezbollah had launched hundreds of projectiles from the ridge toward Israeli civilians and soldiers, and that troops were operating against launch infrastructure in the area.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited troops along Israel's northern border on Friday, accompanied by Katz, where they received briefings on military activities and met with field brigade commanders. The capture followed one of the heaviest days of Hezbollah fire toward northern Israel since an April ceasefire, prompting school closures and restrictions on Saturday.

Israeli forces have expanded operations beyond previous boundaries, crossing the Litani River, which previously served as a de facto boundary between the two countries. The military designated the area between the Litani and Zahrani Rivers as a combat zone. Israeli troops have also been operating near Nabatiyeh, a major Hezbollah stronghold, with the group reporting clashes in several towns north of the river.

The Lebanese Health Ministry reported that 3,371 people have died in the country since March, including both civilians and combatants. The Israeli army announced that 25 Israeli military personnel have been killed since early March, with one soldier killed by a Hezbollah explosive drone in southern Lebanon.

The advance takes place despite a nominal ceasefire in place since April and just before planned talks at the US State Department scheduled for June 2 and 3. Some residents have already evacuated the area due to intense strikes, though people remain in many towns across the region.

cards.headline: 11 Workers Dead After Chemical Tank Collapse at Washington Paper Mill
cards.teaser: All victims have been identified following the tank implosion at a Longview facility operated by Nippon.
cards.body:
Eleven workers died after a chemical tank collapsed at a paper mill in Longview, Washington. Officials have recovered and identified all of the victims from the Nippon mill facility.

The incident involved a tank implosion that released chemicals at the industrial site. Longview officials worked to recover all nine workers who were initially reported missing, bringing the total death toll to eleven. The names of all workers killed in the chemical spill have been released to families.

cards.headline: UN blacklists Israeli and Russian forces for sexual violence
cards.teaser: The United Nations added Israeli and Russian security forces to its annual list of parties credibly suspected of sexual violence during conflict.
cards.body:
The United Nations added Israeli and Russian security forces for the first time to its annual blacklist documenting sexual violence during conflict. The report released Friday includes allegations of rape against detained Palestinians.

The U.N. lists 77 government and non-government parties in countries credibly suspected of patterns of rape or other forms of sexual violence. This marks the first time Israeli and Russian forces have appeared on the annual roster.

cards.headline: Colombia holds presidential election amid tensions with US
cards.teaser: Colombians vote in a presidential election following months of public disputes between President Gustavo Petro and US President Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Colombia held a presidential election that could reshape the country's relationship with the United States. The vote took place following months of public conflict between current left-wing President Gustavo Petro and US President Donald Trump.

The election outcome will be significant in determining Colombia's future diplomatic direction with Washington, particularly given the tensions that have characterized recent exchanges between the two leaders.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo prompts warning from medical charity
cards.teaser: Médecins Sans Frontières describes the Ebola spread in Democratic Republic of Congo as deeply alarming as the WHO chief visits the affected region.
cards.body:
The medical charity Médecins Sans Frontières has warned that Ebola transmission in the Democratic Republic of Congo is deeply alarming, with the virus continuing to spread through certain areas of the country.

The World Health Organization has estimated the outbreak's death rate at between 30% and 50% among confirmed cases. The WHO chief arrived in the region most severely affected by the outbreak to support containment efforts, underscoring international concern about the virus's spread and the humanitarian challenges facing affected communities.

cards.headline: More than 280 arrested in Paris after Champions League celebrations turn violent
cards.teaser: French police detained hundreds nationwide after Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League victory over Arsenal sparked unrest and clashes.
cards.body:
More than 280 people were arrested in Paris following Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League victory over Arsenal. Thousands of police officers deployed across the city to manage crowds as celebrations turned violent, with fans firing flares and clashing with authorities who responded with teargas.

The unrest centered around PSG's Parc de Princes stadium in western Paris, where over 40,000 supporters gathered to watch the match on giant screens. PSG secured their second consecutive Champions League title by defeating Arsenal on penalties in Budapest.

cards.headline: Japan defense minister rejects militarism claims, criticizes China's military expansion
cards.teaser: Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi denied accusations of neo-militarism while making pointed remarks about China's arsenal.
cards.body:
Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi rejected Chinese accusations of new militarism, defending Japan's military strengthening as necessary and appropriate. He criticized China for expanding its arsenal without sufficient transparency, while asserting that Japan should be viewed as a peace-loving nation.

Koizumi's remarks represent some of Tokyo's most direct statements in the ongoing dispute over Japan's defense buildup. Under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, Japan has accelerated its shift toward a more active defense posture, moving away from its post-World War II pacifist approach with U.S. backing.

cards.headline: Five rescued from flooded cave in Laos after week-long ordeal
cards.teaser: Divers freed five people from a flooded cave in Laos after more than a week, with rescue operations continuing for two others still missing.
cards.body:
Rescue teams have freed five men from a flooded cave in Laos where they became trapped while searching for gold. The first person was rescued on Friday, followed by four additional survivors freed through a hazardous operation that required divers to navigate narrow, muddy tunnels filled with sharp rocks.

Two of the seven men who entered the cave on May 20 remain missing. Rescue efforts continue as teams work to drain water from the passages and navigate collapse hazards to locate the remaining individuals.

cards.headline: Israeli soldiers describe indiscriminate operations in Gaza despite ceasefire
cards.teaser: Israeli military personnel gave rare accounts to media outlets describing ongoing violence in Gaza, with one calling the ceasefire a joke.
cards.body:
Israeli soldiers have provided rare firsthand accounts to the Associated Press and The Economist describing ongoing military operations in Gaza. One soldier directly challenged the ceasefire characterization, saying "to call it a ceasefire is a joke." The accounts detail continued military actions in the territory despite the declared ceasefire.

News outlets including Common Dreams have characterized these soldier testimonies as describing indiscriminate killings in Gaza. The accounts represent an uncommon public break from Israeli military personnel regarding operations in the territory.

Longview officials worked to recover all nine workers who were initially reported missing, bringing the total death toll to eleven. The names of all workers killed in the chemical spill have been released to families.

cards.headline: Protests Turn Violent at New Jersey Immigration Detention Facility
cards.teaser: Demonstrators clashed with police outside Delaney Hall as a hunger strike by detainees entered its ninth day.
cards.body:
Demonstrations outside Delaney Hall immigration detention center in Newark intensified as a hunger and labor strike by detained immigrants entered its ninth day. The detainees were demanding improved conditions and medical care.

On Saturday, the scene grew more tense when Trump supporters gathered outside the facility with signs and chants backing ICE. State police set up barricades as the two groups of protesters faced off across the barriers, with supporters of the detained immigrants and ICE backers exchanging heated words.

cards.headline: Bus Driver Charged After Crash Kills Family of Four Heading to Wedding
cards.teaser: Five people died in the Virginia crash on Interstate 95, including a family traveling to a wedding ceremony.
cards.body:
A charter bus driver has been charged with involuntary manslaughter after a crash on Interstate 95 in Virginia killed five people. Among the dead was a family of four who were traveling to a wedding.

A survivor described the bus as traveling at high speed before the collision. Transportation Secretary Duffy pointed to the driver's language in discussing the fatal crash. The incident has raised questions about charter bus safety and driver qualifications on major highways.

cards.headline: Spurs Defeat Thunder in Game 7, Advance to NBA Finals
cards.teaser: San Antonio beat the defending champion Oklahoma City Thunder 111-103 to win the Western Conference.
cards.body:
Victor Wembanyama led the San Antonio Spurs to a stunning 111-103 victory over the Oklahoma City Thunder in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals. The win propels San Antonio to the NBA Finals despite facing the defending champions, who had entered the playoffs as heavy favorites.

The Spurs will now take on the New York Knicks for the league title, with Game 1 scheduled for Wednesday in San Antonio.

cards.headline: White House Releases Trump Physical Exam Results
cards.teaser: The president's doctor says he is in excellent health but recommends weight loss and more exercise.
cards.body:
President Trump remains in excellent health, according to a memo released by the White House from his physician, Dr. Sean Barbabella. The examination found strong cardiac, pulmonary, neurological and overall physical function. However, Trump is dealing with lower leg swelling and benign hand bruising.

The results come after Trump's fourth hospital visit during his second term, which took place at Walter Reed medical center.

cards.headline: California Governor's Race Shows Becerra Gaining Ground
cards.teaser: A new poll shows Xavier Becerra pulling ahead in the crowded field, with Tom Steyer and Rick Hilton close behind.
cards.body:
Xavier Becerra has gained support in the latest polling for California's governor's race, with Tom Steyer and Rick Hilton trailing not far behind. The contest features what analysts describe as weak Democratic front-runners and insurgent Republicans.

California is bracing for what observers call its most turbulent election in years. The race has been marked by chaos, with polls showing a fluid and unpredictable contest. Democratic candidates face challenges from Republican challengers in what has traditionally been a solidly blue state.

cards.headline: China factory activity stalls as demand weakens
cards.teaser: Manufacturing activity in China remained flat in May, raising questions about the health of the world's second-largest economy.
cards.body:
China's factory activity showed no growth in May as demand weakened, according to purchasing managers index data. The manufacturing PMI indicates a slowdown in industrial production, serving as a warning sign for the broader Chinese economy.

The country's non-manufacturing PMI rose slightly to 50.1 in May. The stalling factory activity comes as China faces ongoing economic headwinds and questions about the sustainability of its growth trajectory.

cards.headline: SoftBank to invest up to $87.5 billion in French AI data centers
cards.teaser: SoftBank pledged a major investment to build AI data center facilities in France that would become Europe's biggest such operation.
cards.body:
SoftBank announced plans to invest up to 75 billion euros to build AI data centers in France, creating Europe's largest AI facility. Chairman Masayoshi Son confirmed the commitment, which will develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity.

The investment marks a major expansion of AI infrastructure in Europe, addressing the continent's growing need for computing power to train and deploy artificial intelligence systems.

cards.headline: New car sales decline as one million buyers exit market
cards.teaser: The U.S. new car market has lost approximately one million buyers, with sales falling for the eighth consecutive month.
cards.body:
Auto sales in the United States dropped for the eighth straight month as one million potential new car buyers disappeared from the market. The decline affects manufacturers even as they continue reporting profits, according to industry data.

Electric vehicle demand has collapsed as part of the broader sales downturn. Drivers are feeling financial pressure, making new car purchases increasingly difficult for many Americans who might have bought vehicles in previous years.

cards.headline: Blue Origin receives national security contract hours before rocket explosion
cards.teaser: Blue Origin secured a national security launch task order shortly before a New Glenn rocket exploded at its Florida facility.
cards.body:
Blue Origin received a national security launch task order just hours before one of its New Glenn rockets exploded during a test at Cape Canaveral in Florida. The massive fireball destroyed the launchpad during a scheduled "hotfire" test, with the explosion visible as an orange sky from over 100 miles away in Fort Pierce.

No personnel were harmed in the incident, which Blue Origin described as an anomaly. The company has since regained access to the launchpad. The explosion creates a setback for Blue Origin as it competes with SpaceX, and potentially impacts NASA's plans to build a lunar base and return humans to the moon within the next two years.

cards.headline: United Airlines flight diverted after passenger attempts to breach cockpit
cards.teaser: A United Airlines flight from Chicago to Minneapolis was diverted when a passenger allegedly tried to access the cockpit, forcing a hijacking alert.
cards.body:
A United Airlines flight heading to Minneapolis was diverted to Madison, Wisconsin, after a passenger became unruly and attempted to breach the cockpit. The incident triggered a hijacking alert, and the man was arrested when the plane landed.

The FBI was investigating the incident, though no criminal charges had been filed at the time of reporting.

cards.headline: China's drug development advances, raising U.S. competitiveness concerns
cards.teaser: Clinical trials from China are drawing attention at an international oncology conference as the country's biotech industry grows rapidly.
cards.body:
Chinese clinical trials drew significant attention at an international oncology conference in Chicago, underscoring China's growing prominence in pharmaceutical research. The country's expanding biotechnology sector is prompting concerns about the erosion of U.S. leadership in drug development.

China's advancing capabilities in life sciences and biotechnology represent a notable shift in the global pharmaceutical landscape. The visibility of Chinese research at major medical conferences reflects substantial investments in the sector and reflects changing dynamics in international drug development.

hero.headline: Meteor explodes over Massachusetts, causes sonic boom heard across New England
hero.body:
A meteor exploded over northeastern Massachusetts and southeastern New Hampshire on Saturday afternoon, producing a powerful sonic boom that reverberated across the region, according to Nasa. The space agency confirmed the event occurred just after 2pm local time.

The fireball was traveling at approximately 75,000 miles per hour at an altitude of about 40 miles when it broke apart in the atmosphere. The explosion released energy equivalent to 300 tons of TNT, Nasa's deputy news chief Jennifer Dooren said in a statement to AFP.

The blast created loud booms that were heard and felt by hundreds of people across a wide geographic area. Reports of the sonic boom came from Massachusetts, New Hampshire, and surrounding regions as the shock waves traveled outward from the explosion site.

When meteoroids enter Earth's atmosphere at high speeds, they create visible streaks of light commonly called shooting stars. In this case, the incoming space rock was large enough and moving fast enough that it produced significant effects that were noticed by many residents across the northeastern United States.

According to Nasa's website, most space rocks smaller than a football field will break apart when entering Earth's atmosphere. Though rare, some can explode in the air as this meteor did. Each year, approximately 17,000 meteorites fall to Earth, though most burn up during atmospheric entry or land in unpopulated areas.

The Saturday explosion followed a similar event in Ohio earlier in the week. A meteor over Ohio created a large boom that was felt as far away as Pennsylvania on Tuesday morning. That meteor, which was 2 meters in diameter and weighed about 6 tons, entered the atmosphere at around 9am local time. Residents described the sound as similar to fireworks that "lingered and rumbled like thunder." The National Weather Service's Cleveland office confirmed satellite data suggesting the boom resulted from a meteor.

In that Ohio incident, the meteor was traveling at 45,000 miles per hour before breaking apart over Valley City. Fragments continued southward, producing meteorites in the vicinity of Medina County. Despite the weight of the space rock, Nasa classified it as a small asteroid. Brian Mitchell, an NWS meteorologist, told the Associated Press that while small fragments might reach the ground, much of the meteor would have burned up in the atmosphere.

No reports of damage or injuries have emerged from either meteor event. Such occurrences, while startling to residents who experience the sonic booms, typically happen at altitudes high enough to prevent ground impact damage. The explosions represent the kind of celestial events that periodically remind people of the active space environment surrounding Earth.

cards.headline: Microsoft threatens legal action against security researchers over exploit disclosures
cards.teaser: Microsoft is facing criticism after threatening legal action and blocking a researcher's GitHub account.
cards.body:
Microsoft is facing criticism from the cybersecurity community over how it has handled zero-day exploit disclosures. A researcher using the name Nightmare Eclipse publicly posted proof-of-concept exploit code and engaged in a public dispute with the company. Microsoft responded by blocking the researcher's GitHub account and involving law enforcement.

Security researcher Kevin Beaumont highlighted Microsoft's aggressive response as noteworthy. The researcher reported feeling humiliated by Microsoft's actions and expressed concern that the company's threats could have serious consequences for their life and career. The incident has drawn broader criticism from multiple members of the security community regarding Microsoft's approach to vulnerability disclosures.

cards.headline: First Windows PC with Nvidia processors to launch next week
cards.teaser: Nvidia will debut its first laptop processors for Windows PCs at an industry event.
cards.body:
Nvidia will debut its first Windows PC processor next week at an industry event featuring Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm. The N1X laptop processors mark Nvidia's expansion into the PC processor market, moving beyond its core graphics chip business.

Nvidia has been building anticipation on social media ahead of what the company expects to be one of its largest events of the year.

cards.headline: SoftBank plans up to $75 billion investment in French data centers
cards.teaser: The Japanese firm announced plans to develop and operate 5 gigawatts of data center capacity in France.
cards.body:
SoftBank plans to invest up to €75 billion in French data centers, with the goal of developing and operating up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity in the country.

The investment represents a significant expansion of data infrastructure in France as demand for computing resources continues to grow.

cards.headline: Xbox delays Fable release to February 2027
cards.teaser: Microsoft pushed back the launch of its fantasy game to avoid competing with Grand Theft Auto VI.
cards.body:
Xbox announced a delay for Fable, moving the game's release to February 2027. The postponement marks another delay for the fantasy title, which Microsoft has been developing for several years.

The decision appears aimed at avoiding a direct collision with the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. By moving to early 2027, Microsoft hopes to give Fable a better chance in the market rather than releasing it alongside one of the most anticipated games in years.

cards.headline: James Bond game 007 First Light achieves strong early sales
cards.teaser: The new James Bond video game sold well in its first 24 hours and draws comparisons to Hitman and Uncharted.
cards.body:
The video game 007 First Light became a sales hit, achieving strong numbers in its first 24 hours of availability. Multiple outlets described the game as combining elements of the Hitman stealth series with the adventure style of Uncharted.

Reviewers said the game represents James Bond's brightest future in the gaming space. The title has been called the James Bond game fans have been waiting for, suggesting it successfully captures the spy franchise in interactive form.

cards.headline: AC unveils new Cobra sports car with 720 horsepower
cards.teaser: Britain's oldest active carmaker released a production model powered by a Ford V8 engine.
cards.body:
Britain's oldest active carmaker has officially introduced its new Cobra Coupe, a two-seater sports car powered by a supercharged Ford 5.0-liter V8 engine. The vehicle produces up to 720 horsepower, with certain configurations reaching 799 horsepower.

Priced between $315,000 and $500,000 depending on the specific setup, the modern Cobra represents AC's vision for a high-performance supercar that honors the brand's storied heritage of building powerful sports cars.

hero.headline: Amanda Serrano ties women's boxing knockout record
hero.teaser: Serrano stopped Cheyenne Hanson in the second round to equal the all-time record for most knockouts in women's boxing history.
hero.body:
Amanda Serrano tied Christy Martin's record for most knockouts in women's boxing history with a second-round stoppage of Cheyenne Hanson in Texas. Serrano retained her WBA and WBO featherweight titles in the victory.

The knockout moved Serrano level with Martin's mark set over a career that spanned more than two decades. Serrano also retained her two world championship belts with the win.

cards.headline: PSG wins second straight Champions League title
cards.teaser: Paris Saint-Germain defeated Arsenal in a penalty shootout to become just the second team to win back-to-back Champions League titles.
cards.body:
Paris Saint-Germain won their second consecutive Champions League title on Saturday, defeating Arsenal in a penalty shootout during the final in Budapest. The French club became only the second team in the competition's history to achieve back-to-back championships.

For Arsenal, the loss came in their first Champions League final appearance in 20 years. PSG's victory marks another milestone in their dominant run through European club soccer's premier tournament.

cards.headline: Spurs eliminate defending champion Thunder, advance to NBA Finals
cards.teaser: The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Oklahoma City Thunder 111-103 in Game 7 of the Western Conference finals on Saturday night at Paycom Center, eliminating the .
cards.body:
The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Oklahoma City Thunder 111-103 in Game 7 of the Western Conference finals on Saturday night, ending the reigning champions' title defense. Victor Wembanyama led the Spurs with a strong performance, propelling San Antonio to the NBA Finals for the first time since 2014.

The Spurs will now face the New York Knicks in the Finals, with Game 1 scheduled for Wednesday in San Antonio. The victory marks a significant achievement for the young Spurs team, particularly for Wembanyama, who has emerged as a premier talent in his second season.

cards.headline: Claude Lemieux's brain donated for CTE research
cards.teaser: The former NHL player's family said his brain will be donated to Boston University's CTE Center to study long-term effects of repetitive brain injuries.
cards.body:
Claude Lemieux's brain is being donated to the Boston University CTE Center, his family announced Saturday. The donation will support research into chronic traumatic encephalopathy and the long-term effects of repetitive brain injuries.

Lemieux had a 21-season NHL career, winning four Stanley Cup championships with three different teams. The Boston University center focuses on studying brain trauma in contact sport athletes.

cards.headline: Transgender athlete AB Hernandez wins California state track titles
cards.teaser: The Jurupa Valley senior won two state championships at the California track and field meet amid protests.
cards.body:
AB Hernandez, a transgender senior from Jurupa Valley, won two state titles at the California state track and field championships, closing out her high school career.

The event drew protests, though observers noted they were more subdued than demonstrations at earlier competitions this season.

cards.headline: Caitlin Clark held to six points in Fever loss
cards.teaser: The rookie star struggled with her shooting in an 100-84 defeat to the Fire.
cards.body:
Caitlin Clark struggled offensively as the Indiana Fever fell to the Fire 100-84 on Saturday night. The rookie star was held to just six points in the loss.

Clark's shooting performance was well below her season average, marking one of her worst offensive outings of the year.

cards.headline: Fernando Tatis Jr. hits first home run of season
cards.teaser: The Padres outfielder ended the longest homer drought in MLB with a 451-foot solo shot against the Nationals.
cards.body:
Fernando Tatis Jr. ended Major League Baseball's longest home run drought with a 451-foot solo shot to left field against the Washington Nationals. The blast marked his first homer of the season.

Tatis's power outage had been notably unusual for the slugger, who has previously hit 30 or more home runs in multiple seasons.

hero.headline: Alaskan Bush People Star Matt Brown Dead at 42
hero.body:
Matt Brown, a star of the reality television series Alaskan Bush People, has died at age 42. His brother Noah helped pull his body from a river, according to reports.

Brown had been spotted near a river where police say a man went missing. His brother Bear confirmed the death, though official details about the circumstances have not been released.

Brown appeared on the Discovery Channel series Alaskan Bush People, which followed his family living in remote areas of Alaska. The show documented the Brown family's attempt to live off the grid in the wilderness.

The series premiered in 2014 and ran for multiple seasons, with Matt Brown appearing as one of the central family members. The show gained a following for its portrayal of the family's unconventional lifestyle in the Alaskan wilderness.

Matt Brown had been open about personal struggles in previous years, though specific details about his recent circumstances were not immediately available. The Brown family has been in the public eye through the reality series for over a decade.

Brown's brother Noah was involved in the recovery effort when the body was found in the river. The family has not released an official statement about the death beyond the confirmation from Bear Brown.

The Discovery Channel has not yet commented on Brown's death. The show has continued to air despite various challenges the family has faced over the years, including the death of family patriarch Billy Brown in 2021.

Matt Brown was one of seven Brown siblings featured on the program. The show has documented the family through relocations and personal hardships while maintaining their commitment to living away from modern society.

cards.headline: Italy Bans Kanye West and Travis Scott Concerts Over Security Concerns
cards.teaser: Italian authorities have canceled July concerts by Kanye West and Travis Scott at a northern Italy venue.
cards.body:
Italian authorities have cancelled a Kanye West concert scheduled for July 18 at the RCF Arena in Reggio Emilia, citing public order and safety issues. The city's prefect, Salvatore Angieri, made the decision following concerns raised by the local Jewish community about West's previous antisemitic remarks.

The cancellation affects the Pulse of Gaia festival performance by the 48-year-old rapper, who changed his name to Ye in 2021.

cards.headline: Brad Pitt's Son Files to Drop Actor's Last Name
cards.teaser: Maddox Jolie-Pitt, son of Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie, has filed to remove his father's surname.
cards.body:
Maddox, the son of Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie, has filed to drop the Pitt surname. The legal action reflects the ongoing estrangement between the actor and some of his children following his separation from Jolie.

Brad Pitt was photographed in Paris with girlfriend Ines de Ramon shortly after news of the name change became public.

cards.headline: Love Island USA Removes Cast Member Over Racial Slur
cards.teaser: The reality show has dismissed Vasana Montgomery after social media posts surfaced showing use of a racial slur.
cards.body:
Love Island USA has removed cast member Vasana Montgomery from the show following the discovery of social media posts in which she used the n-word. She will not appear when the series returns to Peacock on June 2.

This is the second consecutive year that Love Island USA has dismissed a contestant for using a racial slur. The show found the problematic posts just days before the season premiere was set to air.

cards.headline: Jay-Z Performs at Philadelphia's Roots Picnic
cards.teaser: The rapper headlined the Roots Picnic in Philadelphia, joined by Jazmine Sullivan, Bilal, and Meek Mill.
cards.body:
Jay-Z headlined the Roots Picnic in Philadelphia, bringing New York influences to the event. The performance featured guest appearances by Jazmine Sullivan, Bilal, and Meek Mill.

The rapper had changed his streaming name from Jay-Z to its original spelling, JA-Z, in recent months ahead of the show. The concert marked a major headlining appearance for the artist, who incorporated multiple collaborators into the performance.

cards.headline: Donald Trump Offers to Perform at Freedom 250 Concert
cards.teaser: The former president said he would perform himself at the anniversary event after artists withdrew from the series.
cards.body:
Donald Trump has offered to personally perform at the Freedom 250 Concert, stating that only great patriots would be invited. The offer comes after several artists withdrew from the anniversary concert series, citing concerns that the event would be political in nature. Among those who backed out were Young MC, Poison frontman Bret Michaels, and country singer Martina McBride.

Following the artist withdrawals, Trump suggested canceling the music performances at the Great American State Fair altogether. Vanilla Ice, who remains scheduled to perform, has defended his participation, arguing that music should not be subject to political rules.

cards.headline: Morgan Wallen Flips Piano During Denver Concert
cards.teaser: The country singer appeared upset with the instrument during a performance of Sand in My Boots.
cards.body:
Morgan Wallen flipped over a piano during a performance in Denver. The country star appeared angry with the instrument while performing his song Sand in My Boots onstage.

The incident occurred during Wallen's concert in the Colorado city. The artist has not publicly commented on what prompted the action during the performance.

hero.headline: Trump requests changes to Iran deal his negotiators reached
hero.body:
President Trump has asked for several amendments to a deal framework his negotiators reached with Iranian counterparts, according to administration officials. The president wants the agreement finalized soon but is seeking to strengthen key provisions, particularly around Iran's nuclear program.

Trump's request has launched another round of negotiations between the parties that could extend several days. The tentative agreement reached this week would extend the current ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz if approved.

Trump announced on Saturday that an agreement had been "largely negotiated" after calls with Pakistani mediators, Gulf allies, and Israel. He posted on his social media platform that "final aspects and details" of a "memorandum of understanding" were still being discussed and would be announced shortly.

According to reports, the draft agreement includes provisions that the strait would reopen without tolls during a 60-day ceasefire extension, while Iran would be able to sell oil freely. Negotiations on curbing Iran's nuclear program would occur over 30 to 60 days. In exchange, the U.S. would lift its blockade on Iranian ports.

However, Iran's Fars news agency, which is close to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, disputed Trump's characterization of progress. The agency reported that "the management of the Strait, determining the route, time, method of passage, and issuing permits will continue to be the monopoly and discretion of the Islamic Republic of Iran," and said Trump's assertion that an agreement was nearly final was "inconsistent with reality."

Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif congratulated Trump on his peace efforts and said Pakistan hoped to host another round of talks between the U.S. and Iran soon. Pakistan's army chief, Syed Asim Munir, has been a key figure in the negotiations, holding recent meetings in Tehran with Iranian leaders.

Trump has described his negotiation strategy as conditional, telling media outlets he would only sign a deal "where we get everything we want," adding that if an agreement was not reached, the U.S. would begin striking Iran again.

The potential deal has sparked criticism from Republican hawks, particularly former officials from Trump's first term. Mike Pompeo, who served as CIA director and secretary of state, denounced the rumored terms as too similar to the 2015 nuclear deal negotiated under President Barack Obama, which Trump withdrew from in 2018.

Former Obama negotiators defended the approach differently. Robert Malley responded to criticism by stating that while the current deal might not follow the exact path his team would have taken, "if this deal brings an end to an unlawful, unjustifiable war, to the senseless loss of life and destruction, and to the cascading global economic fallout, I am quite sure we'd willingly accept it over the alternative."

The timing for final approval remains uncertain as negotiations continue.

cards.headline: Zelensky warns of major Russian attacks within 48 hours
cards.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said intelligence shared by the U.S. and European allies indicates Russia will launch major attacks in the next two days.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is preparing for a significant Russian military attack expected within the next 48 hours, based on intelligence from the U.S. and European allies. He anticipates the strikes could occur at night, either immediately or within the following day.

Zelensky warned of major attacks coming from Russia in the near term.

cards.headline: Justice Department seeks judge's removal from Georgia election case
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors asked a judge to recuse herself from a lawsuit against Georgia election officials after she attended an event honoring Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis.
cards.body:
The Justice Department asked a federal judge to recuse herself from overseeing the department's lawsuit against Georgia election officials. Prosecutors filed the request in the U.S. District Court on Friday.

The department argues the judge's attendance at an event honoring Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis raises questions about her ability to remain impartial. The recusal motion centers on whether the appearance creates a conflict of interest in the ongoing case.

cards.headline: UN blacklists Israeli and Russian forces for sexual violence
cards.teaser: The United Nations added Israeli and Russian security forces to its annual list of parties credibly suspected of sexual violence during conflict.
cards.body:
The United Nations added Israeli and Russian security forces for the first time to its annual blacklist documenting sexual violence during conflict. The report released Friday includes allegations of rape against detained Palestinians.

The U.N. lists 77 government and non-government parties in countries credibly suspected of patterns of rape or other forms of sexual violence. This marks the first time Israeli and Russian forces have appeared on the annual roster.

cards.headline: Prosecutor exits criminal case against James Comey
cards.teaser: The federal prosecutor who secured an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey for allegedly threatening President Trump has stepped down from the case.
cards.body:
The federal prosecutor who secured an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey has stepped down, according to a recent court filing. Comey was indicted for allegedly threatening the life of President Trump in a since-deleted social media post of seashells.

A notice of substitution filed in the Eastern District of North Carolina on Friday stated that Matthew, the lead prosecutor, will no longer handle the case. The filing indicates a different attorney will take over prosecution duties.

cards.headline: Immigrant detainees sue over conditions at Texas ICE facility
cards.teaser: Detainees at an El Paso immigration facility accuse the federal government of inhumane treatment at Camp East Montana.
cards.body:
A class-action lawsuit filed against Immigration and Customs Enforcement accuses the agency of violating detainees' human and constitutional rights at Camp East Montana in El Paso, Texas—the largest immigration detention facility in the United States. Four detainees filed the complaint on behalf of all current and future civil detainees at the facility.

The lawsuit alleges multiple serious problems including inadequate medical and mental health care, inappropriate use of force, and excessive solitary confinement. Detainees also reported inadequate food, disease outbreaks, unsanitary living conditions, and sexual harassment by guards. Legal organizations brought the class-action complaint challenging what they characterize as dire conditions at the facility.

cards.headline: New Jersey governor deploys state police to immigration detention protests
cards.teaser: Gov. Mikie Sherrill deployed state police to maintain order outside a Newark immigration detention center after escalating protests.
cards.body:
New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill and Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin found common ground after the governor deployed state police to maintain order outside a Newark immigration detention center. The facility has been the site of escalating protests.

Sherrill said New Jersey police officers have responded to protests taking place outside the detention center. The deployment came after tensions increased at the site.
